static_traits.name: Chen Hao
static_traits.social_status: Having supportive roommates, but not yet discussing comic-related Anxiety with them; at work, Distraction over choosing reading material affects customer interactions
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no previous similar problems; no previous psychotherapy history
static_traits.language_features: Clear thinking, organized expression, highly cooperative; able to notice and describe automatic thoughts and worries; emotionally stable (neutral)

basic_info.main_problem: 'I will never be able to finish reading all the comics I want', thus feeling overwhelmed and Anxious.
basic_info.core_demands: The oppressive feeling of 'never catching up' undermines enjoyment of the comic hobby and causes Significant anxiety; hoping to reduce this Anxiety through counseling and recover the joy of reading.
growth_experiences: Started working at a comic bookstore two years ago, surrounded daily by huge numbers of old and new comics; since then 'never catching up' Anxiety and oppressive feelings gradually emerged; reading turned from enjoyment into a source of pressure.

The client holds strong passion for comics, but facing massive content and continuous updates, worries of 'if I cannot keep up I will miss great stories' emerged, which gradually became internalized as a stable Anxiety-triggering factor.

core_beliefs: If I cannot do what I love completely and without omission, it means I am not good enough/will miss important experiences
To truly enjoy and love something, one must 'keep up with everything'

special_situations.event: When working at a comic book store, surrounded by a vast number of new and old comics and continuously released new works
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot keep up with all new releases and read all the important ones, I will miss great stories, proving I am not committed enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Making detailed reading lists and plans, constantly comparing and weighing among titles to try to cover 'everything'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never catch up; I will miss a lot of great content.

special_situations.event: Thinking of the huge unread list after finishing each comic
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only by reading everything I want to read is my reading complete and worthwhile
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Immediately expanding the reading list, speeding up the pace, shortening reading time to seek 'coverage'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: There is too much I have not read; I am constantly falling behind.

special_situations.event: Tries to manage choices with a strict reading schedule and checklist
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Through tighter planning, one can achieve complete control over the vast content
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Over-planning and quantified goals, using completion volume as the standard of self-evaluation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: The plan is so long; I will never finish it in this lifetime.

special_situations.event: When needing to help customers at work or face new arrivals
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not make the optimal reading choice right now, it will cause irreversible loss and regret
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Being distracted at work by comparing and picking the next comic, avoiding current tasks
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I choose wrong now I will regret it; better think about which book to read.

core_conflict.wish: Longs to gain completeness and a sense of control in a beloved field, so as to enjoy reading with peace of mind and fully
core_conflict.fear: Fearing missing important works, falling behind, and incompleteness, thereby losing a sense of value and enjoyment
defense_goal: Reduces the risk of 'missing out' through excessive planning and control
Continuously monitors and expands lists to gain a sense of safety

object_relations.self_representation: A reader who can never catch up, a self that easily falls behind
object_relations.object_representation: Endless, daunting outside Demands (a massive number of works) that constantly exert pressure

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked about the source of Anxiety or invited to let go of the 'must finish reading' standard
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tends to interpret inner demands for control and completeness as external objective pressure (too much content, must keep up), thereby weakening awareness of 'one's own standards'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gently probing the source and function of their 'must finish reading' standard with an Empathetic and curious tone, reflecting emotions without over-Interpreting, avoiding directly arguing with their reasons.

manifestations: Feeling a heavy burden of choice facing limitless options and continuously updated works
Seeing 'finishing everything' as a way to take control of free choice
Reading gradually shifts from interest and enjoyment to task-like completion and checklist-driven
Focuses on 'quantity/coverage read' rather than the present experience
outcomes: Distracted at work; quality of interaction with customers declines

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Uses 'must/need to finish reading' as an inner criterion to judge whether the self and the reading are 'qualified'
Treats 'keeping up with everything' as a matter-of-course requirement

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently self-evaluating whether one is 'falling behind' or chose the wrong next book
Fear of missing out causes tension and hesitation in reading and work

positive_force: Has a sustained and deep interest in and investment in comics
Willing to seek help and cooperate with the counselor to explore thoughts and emotions
Has some organizational ability (can make lists and plans)
negative_force: Catastrophic 'missing out' worries and FOMO tendencies
Cognitive distortions such as mental filtering, fortune-telling, and overgeneralization Reinforcing Anxiety
High-stimulation situations (workplace continuously exposed to large numbers of new works)
Sleep affected by Anxiety, forming a negative cycle

target_behavior.behavior: Excessive worry and compulsive planning/comparing about 'being unable to finish reading all the comics one wants to read'
antecedent: Stimulated by large amounts of new and old comics and new-arrival information when working at the bookstore
Thinking of the still-unread list after finishing each comic
When facing the choice of the next book to read or new arrivals
Seeing new works released and recommendation notices
target_behavior.core_reason: Fearing missing important works, pursuing completeness and a sense of control; driven by cognitive biases such as mental filtering, fortune-telling, and overgeneralization
target_behavior.function: Avoiding uncertainty and the Anxiety of 'missing out', temporarily gaining a sense of control and certainty
target_behavior.consequence: Rising Anxiety, Difficulty falling asleep, Decreased enjoyment of reading, Distraction at work and impaired performance, declining quality of customer interactions
